data.name: Husein
data.gender_notes: Husein is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Husein is the name of the grandson of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the third Imam of Shia Muslims. The name is derived from the Arabic word 'husn' meaning 'graceful' or 'handsome'. Husein is also known for his generosity and sacrifice. He is revered for his unwavering devotion and courage during the Battle of Karbala. The name Husein is a reminder of the importance of faith, courage, and self-sacrifice.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of devotion, courage, and self-sacrifice.
data.etymology: Husein belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Graceful, Generous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Husein total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_english.name: Husein
in_english.meaning: The name Hussein refers to the name of the grandson of the Prophet Muhammad
in_english.long_meaning: Hussein ibn Ali is a grandson of the Islamic prophet Muhammad and a son of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the fourth Rashidun caliph. He is a central figure in Shia Islam and a martyr in the Battle of Karbala, commemorated annually by Shia Muslims as Ashura. He is also revered in Sunni Islam as a pious and righteous individual.

data.cultural_impact: The name Husein has significant cultural impact for many Muslim communities, particularly for those of Shia background. Husein's story and legacy are a source of inspiration and pride. His martyrdom at Karbala during the Battle of Karbala in 680CE is commemorated annually during the Islamic month of Muharram. The commemoration involves special mourning rituals, known as majlis, which are held at mosques and in private homes. Many works of art, music, and literature have been inspired by Husein's story and legacy, and the name itself is often given as a sign of respect and admiration.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Husein's life and martyrdom serve as a reminder of the importance of sacrifice and selfless devotion to God. His story highlights the virtues of bravery, perseverance, and steadfastness in the face of adversity. Husein's willingness to sacrifice his life and those of his family for the sake of their faith is a source of inspiration and an example of selflessness and devotion. His legacy serves as a reminder of the importance of remaining steadfast in faith, even in the face of seemingly insurmountable odds. Ultimately, the name Husein represents a deep spiritual connection to the Prophet Muhammad and a commitment to upholding the principles of Islam.

historical_references.reference: Husein ibn Ali was the third Imam of Shia Islam and the grandson of Prophet Muhammad. He was martyred in the Battle of Karbala in 61 AH (680 AD) along with his family and close companions while fighting against the Umayyad Caliph Yazid I.
historical_references.context: Battle of Karbala, Martyred with family and companions against Umayyad Caliph Yazid I

historical_references.reference: Husein ibn Ali al-Karim was the fifth Fatimid Caliph in Egypt from 1021 to 1023, succeeding his father Caliph al-Zahir. He was known for his piety and was the last Fatimid Caliph to rule from Egypt, as the caliphate moved to Tunisia under his successors.
historical_references.context: Fifth Fatimid Caliph in Egypt, Known for piety, Last Fatimid Caliph to rule from Egypt
